assessment: Davies et al. present a large-scale field survey of infection status in crabs. Hematodinium sp., a dinoflagellate parasite that impacts crustacean fisheries worldwide. Hematodinium sp., previously thought to render crabs more susceptible to other infectious agents via immunosuppression, was not found to be associated with collateral infections with other disease agents. This study, instead, presents a new framework for Hematodinium-crab interactions; latency of the infection and absence of host immune response may drive the endemic status of Hematodinium sp. infections in crustaceans.
